articles.title: Biosimilars Facing Formulary Adoption Hurdles
articles.summary: Industry expert Christine Johnston discusses the market dynamics and rebate structures causing biosimilars to lose ground on commercial formularies. This trend directly impacts self-funded employers seeking cost-effective alternatives to high-priced biologic drugs through their PBM strategies.
articles.source_line: Source: Managed Healthcare Executive; Mon, 05 Oct 2026 23:25:24 GMT

articles.title: PhRMA Report Attributes $12.8 Billion in 2025 Employer Costs to 340B Program
articles.summary: A new report from PhRMA claims that commercial employers faced $12.8 billion in higher health care costs in 2025 due to the 340B drug pricing program. This highlights the ongoing financial impact of 340B on self-funded plans and underscores why employer advocacy groups and PBMs are closely monitoring program reform and litigation. The findings emphasize the pressure self-funded employers face regarding drug cost drivers tied to institutional pricing disparities.

articles.title: McKesson and CD&R to Acquire Option Care Health for $5.8B
articles.summary: Clayton, Dubilier & Rice and McKesson are acquiring infusion therapy provider Option Care Health in a $5.8 billion deal. This major consolidation in specialty and infusion services significantly impacts the specialty drug distribution and care management landscape relevant to high-cost employer health plan management.
articles.source_line: Source: Fierce Healthcare; Tue, 06 Oct 2026 16:30:00 GMT

articles.title: Mark Cuban's Cost-Plus Enters New Jersey Benefits Market
articles.summary: Mark Cuban's transparent pharmacy benefits model is expanding into New Jersey, challenging traditional PBM pricing structures. This move offers self-funded employers alternative contracting options focused on transparent drug pricing and bypassing traditional spread pricing. The entry signals continued disruption in the PBM market as employers seek out cost-containment strategies.

articles.title: The Disconnect Between Rising Manufacturer Rebates and Employer Pharmacy Costs
articles.summary: Despite increasing manufacturer rebates, self-funded employers continue to see overall pharmacy benefit costs climb. This persistent trend highlights the limitations of traditional rebate-focused PBM pricing models and underscores the urgent need for self-funded plans to demand greater transparency and true cost management.
articles.source_line: Source: Insurance Business; Tue, 06 Oct 2026 11:07:24 GMT

articles.title: Congressional PBM Reform Faces Hurdles Before Reaching Consumers
articles.summary: The article discusses ongoing legislative efforts surrounding pharmacy benefit manager (PBM) reform and the challenges Congress faces in passing impactful policy changes. For self-funded employers and PBMs, this signals continued uncertainty regarding federal oversight, transparency mandates, and drug pricing regulations.
